title: Reservation Stabilizer — multi-tenant burst arbitration and isolation PRD
creator: Asha Kapoor
summary: Introduce a Reservation Stabilizer service and console controls to arbitrate multi-tenant bursts against reserved pools, reduce noisy neighbor effects, and provide predictable isolation guarantees while preserving opportunistic burst capacity.
problem_statement: Customers with reserved Dedicated capacity experience unpredictable tail latency and reservation contention when other tenants burst. Current soft-burst behavior either allows excessive spillback (hurting reserved SLOs) or is too conservative (wasting idle capacity). There is no single control that balances fairness, preemption grace, and credit-based borrowing across tenants with different SLA classes.
objectives: Provide a deterministic arbitration model (Reservation Stabilizer) that enforces reserved tenant isolation targets under burst conditions
Enable safe opportunistic bursting with credit accounting and decay so non-reserved tenants can use spare capacity without violating reserved tenant SLOs
Expose console controls and API flags for reservation headroom, preemption grace windows, and spillback sensitivity
Ship telemetry, dashboards, and playbooks needed for customers and SRE to validate behavior and debug regressions
success_metrics: For top-tier reserved contracts: 95th percentile tail latency under regional surge is <= baseline + 20% within 2 weeks of rollout
Reduction of incidents classified as ‘reserved-tenant degradation due to burst’ by >= 80% versus control group
Percent of spare capacity consumed opportunistically with zero SLO violations >= 60% in steady-state workloads
Operator rollbacks due to stabilization bugs: 0 during canary; <1 per month thereafter
scope_in: Server-side Reservation Stabilizer: arbitration engine that runs in control plane and instructs routing/fallbacks
New tenant-level reservation policy fields (headroom_percent, burst_credit_rate, preempt_grace_seconds, spillback_threshold) in the Dedicated API
Console UI for Stabilizer profile selection and live telemetry view
Telemetry: per-tenant credit ledger, arbitration decisions histogram, preempt events, and SLO violation markers
Canary and rollout automation tied to targeted zones and customer cohorts
scope_out: Changes to model kernels or low-level runtime execution (handled in separate runtime perf initiatives)
A complete rework of billing/contract negotiation for reserved tiers (billing changes will be additive later)
Cross-region global burst negotiation (this PRD only addresses per-region arbitration)
functional_requirements: R1: Reservation Stabilizer must maintain a per-tenant credit ledger that increments during idle periods and decrements while bursting; credit accrual and decay parameters must be configurable per reservation

R2: When cluster utilization crosses spillback_threshold, Stabilizer must compute an arbitration decision that may: throttle opportunistic traffic, route requests to fallback models/regions, or preempt opportunistic allocations after preempt_grace_seconds
R3: API must expose new reservation policy fields: headroom_percent (integer 0-100), burst_credit_rate (tokens/minute), max_burst_quota, preempt_grace_seconds (int), spillback_threshold (float 0-1)
R4: Stabilizer must support policy profiles: conservative, balanced, and aggressive; customers can choose a profile default and override per-reservation
R5: Console must show live credit balance, likely next-preempt ETA, and a toggle to simulate limiting decisions for planning
R6: Service must log all arbitration decisions with trace IDs and attach them to request traces for SLO debugging
R7: Provide an open API for Engineering to query stabilized state for a tenant for audit/telemetry purposes
R8: Implement a soft-fail safe mode: on control-plane outage, default to last-known policy and surface a clear degraded-control-plane alert
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Arbitration decision latency must be < 50ms per decision in the control plane under 99th percentile load
NFR2: Telemetry must be available with <= 30s staleness for console visualization
NFR3: Stabilizer must be horizontally scalable and stateless for decision logic; ledger storage can be strongly consistent key-value store with < 500ms write tail
NFR4: Feature flags must allow per-customer opt-in/opt-out for canary rollouts
NFR5: All policy changes must be auditable and surfaced in tenant audit logs for 365 days
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Unit and integration tests cover credit accrual/decay math with deterministic fixtures

AC2: End-to-end tests simulate a 3-tenant surge scenario (Reserved A, Reserved B, Opportunistic C) and verify Reserved A's p95 latency does not exceed baseline + 20% while opportunistic C uses remaining capacity until preempt_grace_seconds expire
AC3: API schema validated and backwards compatible for existing reservations that do not set new fields (defaults applied server-side)
AC4: Console shows credit balances and a live arbitration timeline in staging for 2 pilot customers

AC5: Telemetry emitted to metrics backend with the following metrics: stabilizer.arbitration_decisions.count, stabilizer.credit_balance{tenant}, stabilizer.preempt_events.count, stabilizer.spillback_events.count
AC6: Canary rollout on two low-risk zones for 48 hours with a control cohort; incidents and SLO regressions reviewed by PM/Eng/SRE; no automatic rollback triggered
AC7: Operator runbook validated in tabletop exercise and leads to correct mitigation steps for 3 common failure modes
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Dev): implement decision engine and API; unit/integration tests; internal staging deployment
Phase 1 (Staging): integrate with routing layer, console UI staging view; invite 2 pilot customers (opt-in)
Phase 2 (Canary): enable for 10% of capacity across two zones; monitor metrics for 72h; run SRE review
Phase 3 (Gradual): 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 weeks with automated rollback if p95 reserved latency breaches threshold
Phase 4 (GA): enable feature flag default for new reservations and expose migration docs for existing customers
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert M2: reserved_tenant_slo_violations.count sudden spike (> 3x baseline) within 15m
Dashboard D1: per-reservation credit balance, recent arbitration decisions, preempt event timeline
Dashboard D2: regional heatmap showing spillback events and opportunistic consumption
operational_playbook: If reserved tenant latency increases: check stabilizer logs for arbitration decisions, verify credit balances, and assess recent opportunistic consumption; if policy misconfiguration found, apply immediate temporary increase to headroom_percent
If control plane unavailable: enable safe mode; inform customers and fallback to last-known policies; follow outage RCA template
If preemptions are causing customer complaints: temporarily increase preempt_grace_seconds for affected tenants and schedule later policy tuning
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect credit math could allow starvation or over-allocation. Mitigation: formal verification tests and time-series fuzzing harness before canary
Risk: Policy complexity confuses customers. Mitigation: provide three curated profiles and a one-click revert to conservative profile
Risk: Telemetry gaps hinder debugging. Mitigation: instrument mandatory decision logging linked to trace IDs and backfill pipeline checks
open_questions: Q1: What is the default headroom_percent we commit to for enterprise SLAs? Suggested: 10% to start, evaluate during pilot
Q2: Should credits be transferable between reservations owned by the same customer? (billing/contract implications)
Q3: Do we offer a marketplace-like opt-in where customers can sell unused credits back to opportunistic pools? (out of scope for initial launch)
stakeholders: Engineering: Noah Zhang (feature lead), Priya Menon (runtime integration)
implementation_notes: Implement decision engine as a new microservice behind control-plane, stateless decision node reading from centralized ledger (consistent KV store)
Routing layer must be able to accept a short-circuit instruction to apply per-request throttles or route to fallback model variant
Ledger should be sharded by tenant-id and expose a light-weight query API for console and e2e tests
Default policies applied server-side for reservations created before GA to maintain backward compatibility
